antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/CountInactiveUsers.php:24 — prints a bare number with no label; the scheduled output in logs/inactive-users.log is an unlabelled integer, weak for the 'shows up in our logs' requirement
tests/Feature/CountInactiveUsersTest.php:10 — global helper function userLoggedInDaysAgo() declared in a Pest file pollutes the global namespace; a factory state is the idiomatic alternative
tests/Feature/CountInactiveUsersTest.php:46-51 — the boundary test uses 90 vs 91 days, which is less precise than a one-second boundary
strengths: Minimal, proportionate: one scope, one small command, one schedule line
Indexes last_login_at, sensible for a daily count query
Modern #[Scope], #[Signature] and #[Description] attributes; uses the Schedule facade in routes/console.php
Validates --days via filter_var with min_range, with a failure exit code and a dataset-driven invalid-input test
Tests the schedule expression and output path; uses freezeTime

antipatterns: routes/console.php:12 — withoutOverlapping(10) is unnecessary ceremony for a single fast count query on a single server and adds a cache-lock dependency
tests/Feature/UsersInactiveCountTest.php:10 — Http::preventStrayRequests() is irrelevant noise; the command makes no HTTP calls
database/migrations/2026_11_07_185238_add_last_login_at_to_users_table.php:12 — ->after() is MySQL-only and there is no index on the queried column
strengths: Labelled output ('Users inactive for 90 days: N') is useful in the scheduled log
Adds a lastLoginAt() factory state, giving idiomatic test setup
Precise boundary test (exactly 90 days vs 90 days plus one second)
Rejects zero, negative, text and decimal --days values with a clear error and a failure exit code; covered by a dataset
Modern #[Scope] and command attributes; the schedule test checks the cron expression and output path; uses a typed closure

v.rationale: The two are nearly identical in core logic (same #[Scope] query, the same attribute-based command and the same Schedule facade entry), and neither has a real bug. Probes for --days=0, huge values, empty, '+30', ' 30' and future logins behaved sensibly in both. impl-2 wins narrowly. Its labelled output serves the stated 'shows up in our logs' purpose better than impl-1's bare integer. Its factory state is more idiomatic than impl-1's global test helper, and its one-second boundary test is more precise. Against impl-2: withoutOverlapping and Http::preventStrayRequests are unneeded ceremony, and it has no index. impl-1 is leaner and adds a useful index, but its log output and test helpers are weaker.
